The fiber API

Source: vignettes/fiber-api.qmd

This vignette is the reference for fiber’s programming interface. It describes every class, slot, read-only property, generic, and method, together with the subsetting (“push-down”) semantics and the coercion rules between fiber classes and the dwiFiber S4 class of the dti package. For a gentler introduction, see the getting started vignette.

The package defines three S7 classes:

  • streamline
  • bundle
  • bundle_set

and a set of generics and functions:

  • Constructors & predicates: streamline(), bundle(), bundle_set(), is_streamline(), is_bundle(), is_bundle_set()
  • Combination: bind_bundles(), bind_bundle_sets()
  • Reparametrisation: reparametrize()
  • Shape descriptors: get_euclidean_length(), get_curvilinear_length(), get_sinuosity(), get_curvature(), get_torsion(), add_shape_descriptors()
  • Distances: compute_hausdorff_distance()
  • Coercion: as_streamline(), as_bundle(), as_bundle_set(), as_dwifiber()

Class: streamline

A streamline represents a single fibre tract as a polyline of 3-D points. It stores three compartments:

Slots

Slot Type / shape Contents
@points P x 3 numeric matrix, columns "X", "Y", "Z" The 3-D coordinates of the P points along the tract.
@point_data named list of numeric vectors, each of length P Per-point scalar attributes (e.g. fractional anisotropy). "X" / "Y" / "Z" are not allowed here.
@streamline_data named list of scalars (length 1, any type) Per-streamline attributes (e.g. mean FA or a character label).

Read-only properties

Property Type Meaning
@n_points integer Number of points (nrow(@points)).
@point_attributes character Names of the entries in @point_data.
@streamline_attributes character Names of the entries in @streamline_data.

Construction 

sl <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = 0:4, Y = 0:4, Z = 0:4),
  point_data = list(FA = runif(5)),
  streamline_data = list(label = "CST")
)
sl
#> 
#> ── Object of class `fiber::streamline()` with 5 points. ──
#> 
#> • Point attributes: "FA"
#> • Streamline attributes: "label"
#> 
sl@n_points
#> [1] 5
sl@point_attributes
#> [1] "FA"

The validator insists that @points is a numeric P x 3 matrix with column names exactly c("X", "Y", "Z"), that every @point_data entry is a numeric vector of length P, and that every @streamline_data entry has length 1.

Method surface

format() returns a cli-formatted string; print() prints it and returns the object invisibly.

Class: bundle

A bundle is an ordered collection of streamline objects, e.g. a tractogram.

Slots

Slot Type / shape Contents
@streamlines list of streamline objects The individual tracts.
@streamline_data named list of vectors, each of length S Per-streamline attributes aggregated at the bundle level. Common keys may be lifted here automatically at construction.
@bundle_data named list of scalars (length 1, any type) Bundle-level metadata.

Read-only properties

Property Type Meaning
@n_streamlines integer Number of streamlines.
@streamline_attributes character Names of the entries in @streamline_data.
@bundle_attributes character Names of the entries in @bundle_data.

Automatic lifting

At construction, any @streamline_data key present in all supplied streamlines is copied into bundle@streamline_data as a length-S vector, and the key is then not stored redundantly in each streamline. Values supplied explicitly via the streamline_data argument take precedence.

sl1 <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = 0:4, Y = 0:4, Z = 0:4),
  streamline_data = list(mean_FA = 0.6, label = "A")
)
sl2 <- streamline(
  points = cbind(X = 1:3, Y = 1:3, Z = 1:3),
  streamline_data = list(mean_FA = 0.7, label = "A")
)
b <- bundle(streamlines = list(sl1, sl2))
b@streamline_data$mean_FA # c(0.6, 0.7) — lifted automatically
#> [1] 0.6 0.7
b@streamline_attributes # c("mean_FA", "label")
#> [1] "mean_FA" "label"

The bundle validator requires every element of @streamlines to be a streamline (with no duplicate names), every @streamline_data entry to have length S, and every @bundle_data entry to have length 1.

Subsetting and push-down

bundle[[i]] extracts the i-th streamline and pushes back the corresponding bundle@streamline_data values into the streamline’s @streamline_data:

b[[1]]@streamline_data$mean_FA # 0.6
#> [1] 0.6

bundle[i] returns a new bundle with only the selected streamlines, preserving @bundle_data and the subset of @streamline_data:

b[1]@streamline_data$mean_FA # c(0.6)
#> [1] 0.6
b[1]@streamline_data$label # "A"
#> [1] "A"

Class: bundle_set

A bundle_set is a collection of bundle objects. It is designed for two closely related use cases: grouping the multiple white-matter bundles of a single subject, or grouping bundles across subjects / sessions in a multi-subject / multi-session study.

Slots

Slot Type / shape Contents
@bundles list of bundle objects (names optional) One element per bundle (e.g. per white-matter bundle of a subject, or per subject / session).
@bundle_data named list of vectors, each of length B Per-bundle attributes aggregated at the set level.
@bundle_set_data named list of scalars (length 1, any type) Set-level metadata.

Read-only properties

Property Type Meaning
@n_bundles integer Number of bundles.
@bundle_attributes character Names of the entries in @bundle_data.
@bundle_set_attributes character Names of the entries in @bundle_set_data.

Names become id_from_input_names

If the input bundles list is named (e.g. list("sub-01" = b1, "sub-02" = b2)), the names are transferred into bundle_set@bundle_data under the key id_from_input_names and the names are then dropped from @bundles.

b_sub01 <- bundle(
  streamlines = list(sl1),
  bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-01")
)
b_sub02 <- bundle(
  streamlines = list(sl2),
  bundle_data = list(subject = "sub-02")
)
bs <- bundle_set(list("sub-01" = b_sub01, "sub-02" = b_sub02))
bs@bundle_data$id_from_input_names # c("sub-01", "sub-02")
#> [1] "sub-01" "sub-02"

As with bundles, common @bundle_data keys are lifted automatically at construction, and the explicit bundle_data argument takes precedence.

Subsetting and push-down

bundle_set[[i]] extracts the i-th bundle and pushes the matching bundle_set@bundle_data values into the bundle’s @bundle_data. bundle_set[i] returns a new bundle_set with @bundle_set_data and the subset of @bundle_data preserved.

bs[["sub-01"]]@bundle_data$subject # "sub-01" (pushed down)
#> [1] "sub-01"
bs[1]@bundle_data$subject # "sub-01"
#> [1] "sub-01"

Predicates

Function Returns TRUE when x is …
is_streamline(x) a streamline
is_bundle(x) a bundle
is_bundle_set(x) a bundle_set 
is_streamline(sl) # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
is_bundle(sl) # FALSE
#> [1] FALSE
is_bundle_set(bs) # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE

Combination

bind_bundles()

bind_bundles(...) combines any mix of streamline and bundle objects into a single flat bundle. bundle_data and streamline_data from the first bundle argument are preserved by default; pass your own via the streamline_data and bundle_data arguments to override. Keys present in only some inputs are NA-padded for the others.

b_all <- bind_bundles(sl1, b)
b_all@n_streamlines # 3
#> [1] 3

bind_bundle_sets()

bind_bundle_sets(...) combines any mix of bundle and bundle_set objects into a single flat bundle_set. Bare bundle arguments may be named to carry their name into the resulting set (with id_from_input_names populated accordingly), or left unnamed. bundle_data from the first bundle_set argument is preserved by default; pass your own via bundle_data or bundle_set_data.

bs_merged <- bind_bundle_sets("sub-A" = b_sub01, bs)
bs_merged@n_bundles # 3
#> [1] 3

Reparametrisation

reparametrize(x, n_points = NULL) resamples coordinates (and any numeric @point_data entries) onto a uniform arc-length grid by linear interpolation.

  • For a streamline, n_points defaults to x@n_points.
  • For a bundle, it defaults to the rounded mean number of points across its streamlines, and every streamline is resampled to the same grid size.
  • For a bundle_set, each bundle is reparametrized independently (defaulting, per bundle, to the rounded mean across that bundle’s streamlines).

Non-numeric @point_data entries are dropped with a warning (they have no natural arc-length interpolant). @streamline_data, @bundle_data, and @bundle_set_data are preserved unchanged.

sl_20 <- reparametrize(sl1, n_points = 20L)
sl_20@n_points # 20
#> [1] 20
b_20 <- reparametrize(b, n_points = 20L)
b_20[[1]]@n_points # 20
#> [1] 20

n_points must be at least 2.

Shape descriptors

Function Returns
get_euclidean_length(x) Straight-line distance between the endpoints (resolution-P independent).
get_curvilinear_length(x) Total arc-length (sum of Euclidean segment lengths).
get_sinuosity(x) Curvilinear / Euclidean ratio (1 = straight; larger = curvier).
get_curvature(x) Per-point curvature profile (length P), via cubic smoothing splines.
get_torsion(x) Per-point torsion profile (length P), via cubic smoothing splines.

get_curvature() and get_torsion() are per-point profile descriptors: they fit smoothing splines to each coordinate along the arc-length abscissa, so they need at least four distinct points and are well defined only where the tract is actually curved. On a perfectly straight segment, curvature is identically zero and torsion (which measures out-of-plane twisting) is undefined (NaN). The helix below is a good curve to illustrate both, because it is genuinely curved in every direction:

sl_curve <- streamline(
  points = cbind(
    X = cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 21)),
    Y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 21)),
    Z = seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 21)
  )
)
# Scalar descriptors are fine on any streamline
get_euclidean_length(sl1)
#> [1] 6.928203
get_curvilinear_length(sl1)
#> [1] 6.928203
get_sinuosity(sl1)
#> [1] 1

# Per-point profiles are meaningful on a truly curved tract
head(get_curvature(sl_curve))
#> [1] 2.547019e-05 2.553796e-02 6.620551e-02 1.142371e-01 1.646170e-01
#> [6] 2.142204e-01
head(get_torsion(sl_curve))
#> [1] -115.1033091    0.5632915    0.4238968    0.4045585    0.4208142
#> [6]    0.4554351

add_shape_descriptors()

add_shape_descriptors(x, descriptors = ...) is an S7 generic with methods for streamline, bundle, and bundle_set. The default descriptors is c("euclidean_length", "curvilinear_length", "sinuosity", "curvature", "torsion").

  • For a streamline, scalar descriptors land in @streamline_data and per-point ones in @point_data.
  • For a bundle, scalar descriptors are stored as length-S vectors in bundle@streamline_data; per-point ones (curvature, torsion) are stored in each individual streamline’s @point_data. Both are accessible via the subsetting push-down.
  • For a bundle_set, the operation is applied per bundle, preserving @bundle_data and @bundle_set_data.

Unknown descriptor names trigger a structured cli::cli_warn() message.

Note that get_curvature() and get_torsion() fit cubic smoothing splines and therefore need a streamline with at least four distinct points (the examples below use 10-point streamlines).

b_long <- bundle(
  streamlines = list(
    streamline(points = cbind(X = 0:9, Y = 0:9, Z = 0:9)),
    streamline(points = cbind(X = 1:10, Y = 1:10, Z = 1:10))
  )
)
b_desc <- add_shape_descriptors(b_long)
names(b_desc@streamline_data)
#> [1] "euclidean_length"   "curvilinear_length" "sinuosity"
names(b_desc[[1]]@point_data)
#> [1] "curvature" "torsion"

Hausdorff distance

compute_hausdorff_distance(x, y = NULL) computes the symmetric Hausdorff distance. It dispatches on four cases:

x y Returns
streamline streamline Scalar: max(d_H(x→y), d_H(y→x)).
bundle NULL dist object (size n) of all pairwise distances within x.
bundle streamline Numeric vector (length n): distance from y to each streamline in x.
bundle bundle dist object over the concatenation of all streamlines of x and y. 
sb <- streamline(points = cbind(X = 0:4, Y = 0:4, Z = 0:4))
sc <- streamline(points = cbind(X = 1:5, Y = 1:5, Z = 1:5))

# streamline x streamline -> scalar
compute_hausdorff_distance(sb, sc)
#> [1] 1.732051

# bundle x missing -> dist object
bd <- bundle(streamlines = list(sb, sc))
as.matrix(compute_hausdorff_distance(bd))
#>          1        2
#> 1 0.000000 1.732051
#> 2 1.732051 0.000000

# bundle x streamline -> vector
compute_hausdorff_distance(bd, sb)
#> [1] 0.000000 1.732051

# bundle x bundle -> combined dist object
bd2 <- bundle(streamlines = list(sc))
as.matrix(compute_hausdorff_distance(bd, bd2))
#>          1        2        3
#> 1 0.000000 1.732051 1.732051
#> 2 1.732051 0.000000 0.000000
#> 3 1.732051 0.000000 0.000000

The core pairwise computation is implemented in C++ (via cpp11). Coordinates are coerced to double precision before being passed to the compiled code, so integer-stored @points matrices (e.g. built from X = 1:5) are handled correctly. Unsupported x types (and invalid y) produce a clear error via the catch-all method.

Coercion

as_streamline()

as_streamline(x) returns a streamline:

  • streamline → returned unchanged (identity).
  • bundle → the sole streamline (errors if the bundle has ≠ 1 streamlines).
  • dwiFiber (from dti) → the single fiber as a streamline (errors if multi-fiber; use as_bundle() instead).

as_bundle()

as_bundle(x) returns a bundle:

  • streamline → a single-element bundle (lossless).
  • bundle → returned unchanged (identity).
  • dwiFiber → each fiber becomes a streamline. Per-point direction vectors (columns 4–6 of @fibers) are stored as @point_data$direction_x/y/z. Tracking metadata (method, minfa, maxangle) become scalars in @bundle_data; vector metadata (ddim, ddim0, voxelext, orientation) are expanded into individual scalar entries (e.g. voxelext_1, voxelext_2, voxelext_3).

as_bundle_set()

as_bundle_set(x) returns a bundle_set:

  • bundle_set → returned unchanged (identity).
  • bundle → a single-element bundle_set; the optional name argument sets the element name.

as_dwifiber()

as_dwifiber(x) converts a streamline or bundle to the dwiFiber S4 class from dti. It requires the dti package to be installed. Per-point directions are taken from @point_data$direction_x/y/z when present, otherwise estimated from the coordinates via finite differences (forward / backward at the ends, central elsewhere), then unit-normalised. Bundled metadata under method, minfa, maxangle, level, and source are transferred to the corresponding dwiFiber slots when present.

Note

Because dti loads the rgl package on startup, calling the coercion functions in an environment without a graphics display can print an rgl warning (e.g. 'rgl.init' failed or X11 error). That warning comes from rgl, not from fiber, and does not affect the conversion.

if (requireNamespace("dti", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dfi <- as_dwifiber(bd)
  class(dfi)
  # round-trip
  as_bundle(dfi)@n_streamlines
}
#> [1] 2

Console output

All three classes provide format() and print() methods that render cli-styled, ANSI-aware summaries (object class, point/bundle counts, and the per-point, per-streamline, per-bundle, and set-level attribute names). print() also returns the object invisibly, and length(), [[, and [ follow the semantics described above.

For the canonical documentation of every generic, method, argument, and return value, see the package reference at https://tractoverse.github.io/fiber/reference/.
